facts.text: Gates Mills was founded by Holsey Gates in 1826, who built the first sawmill that sparked the village’s growth.
The village’s name honors Halsey Gates, the proprietor of a local watermill that powered early industry.
In 1829 a gristmill began operating, marking Gates Mills’ transition from a rural mill community to a thriving village.
The Southwick House Museum, housed in a historic 19th‑century home, preserves artifacts and original furniture donated by the Southwick family.
Gates Mills celebrated its 100th anniversary of incorporation in 2020, a milestone highlighted by a commemorative plaque at Christopher’s Episcopal Church.
The village’s interurban station, once a stop on the old rail line, now sits beside the old water pump and is marked on local maps.
